item.text: I’ve got one meaningful refactor left in the implementation itself: the public API accepts `CharSequence`, but the internals still carry mutability through every helper. I’m going to normalize inputs once at the boundary, simplify the inner types back to immutable `String`, and add a checked-in test file so the behavior checks live in the repo instead of temp harnesses.

I’m editing both the implementation and a new test file now. The implementation change is boundary normalization plus a smaller `SearchPattern`; the new test file will lock in the edge cases we’ve been manually verifying.
The normalization refactor and checked-in test file are in place. I’m compiling both files and running the sample plus the new test class to verify the repository now carries its own behavior checks.
Compilation succeeded. I’m running the sample entrypoint and the new checked-in test class now; if those pass, this pass is complete.

I continued the refactor in [RabinKarp.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/022_rabin_karp/RabinKarp.java:13) by normalizing `CharSequence` inputs to immutable `String` values at the API boundary. That removes mutability concerns from the helper types, lets `SearchPattern` cache its `length`, and simplifies the internal contracts: `SearchPattern`, `SearchState`, `TextWindow`, and `RollingHash` now operate on stable `String` data instead of carrying generic `CharSequence` through every layer.

I also added a checked-in test harness in [RabinKarpTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/022_rabin_karp/RabinKarpTest.java:1) covering repeated matches, overlapping matches, empty patterns, too-long patterns, and non-`String` `CharSequence` inputs.
